_about: Hand-picked, well-known CVEs that Aegis can match offline. Scores and KEV flags checked against NIST NVD on 2026-11-20. ranges: introduced = first affected version, fixed = first safe version (exclusive), last_affected = last affected version (inclusive), exact = only this version. Live NVD lookups add everything else when online.

cves.summary: Path traversal: attackers can read files outside the website folder and, with CGI enabled, run commands. Mass-exploited within days.
The fix for CVE-2021-41773 in 2.4.50 was incomplete: same file-reading / remote command attack still works.
Buffer overflow in mod_lua's request parser can let attackers crash or take over the server.
HTTP request smuggling via mod_proxy: attackers can bypass access controls and reach internal pages.
mod_rewrite escaping flaw lets attackers read files or run code that should not be reachable from the web.
'regreSSHion': a timing bug lets an attacker run code as root on the SSH server without logging in (Linux/glibc).
'Terrapin': an attacker in the network path can silently weaken the security of an SSH connection.
Attackers can find out which usernames exist by timing login attempts, making password guessing easier.
Backdoored release: a login with ':)' in the username opens a root shell on port 6200.
mod_copy lets anyone copy files on the server without logging in, which can be turned into running code.
'Return of the WIZard': a crafted email address lets attackers run commands as root on the mail server.
SMTP smuggling: attackers can send emails that look like they come from your domain.
'Heartbleed': attackers can read the server's memory, including private keys and passwords.
A malicious certificate can make the server loop forever (denial of service).
With nginx + PHP-FPM, a crafted URL lets attackers run code on the server.
PHP-CGI on Windows: a character-encoding trick lets attackers run code. Used by ransomware groups.
PHP-CGI treats parts of the URL as command-line options, letting attackers run code.
IIS 6.0 WebDAV buffer overflow lets attackers take over the server. IIS 6.0 (Windows Server 2003) is long out of support.
Bug in nginx's DNS resolver: a forged DNS answer can crash nginx or possibly run code.
Crafted 'chunked' request causes a stack overflow: crash or remote code execution.
